title: Lydia Beeswax Requirements
subject: Contracts
stem:
Barnabas Wax Co. promptly accepted a signed email from Lydia, who runs a Bible-verse candle studio. The email said: “I offer to buy all the beeswax my studio requires for the next nine months at $18 per slab, shipment every other Friday.” Lydia later asserted that no contract had formed because the email did not list a fixed number of slabs.

Which statement is most accurate?

choices.A: No contract formed unless the court finds $18 per slab was an adequate price.
choices.B: A contract can form because the quantity is measured by Lydia’s good-faith requirements.
choices.C: No contract formed because the email was only a price quote.
choices.D: No contract formed because a requirements quantity is always too indefinite and illusory.

rightExplanation: B is correct. Gold Key: a requirements quantity is not an empty quantity; it is measured by the buyer’s actual good-faith requirements. Silver Key: in a 3-vs-1 no-contract array, do not let “no fixed number” erase a quantity phrase that the stem already gives you. Lydia’s email gives a price, a delivery schedule, goods, duration, and the quantity formula: all beeswax the studio requires. That can support contract formation.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: “Adequate price” is a fabricated formation gate. This needs the consideration-adequacy anchor; without it, keep the doctrine under lawyer confirmation.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: The choice answers the wrong frame. The stem says buyer’s offer plus acceptance; the call asks about the no-fixed-number attack.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: “Always” is the visible overclaim. Requirements terms are exactly the category that makes the absolute suspicious.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text: B remains. No CLASH or CALL needed.

studentScript: Call: most accurate statement. Fixed-number attack. Cut D for always. Cut A with adequacy anchor. Cut C because price quote is the wrong frame. Gold Key: requirements quantity counts by good faith. B remains.

A.signal: The choice makes court price-adequacy review a formation condition.
A.lawyer: Adequacy of price is not an additional formation requirement once consideration exists.

B.signal: This directly answers the missing-fixed-number attack.
B.lawyer: UCC 2-306 validates output and requirements quantities measured by good faith.

C.signal: The stem gives a buyer's offer and acceptance; this choice answers a price-quote question.
C.lawyer: A price-quote rule does not defeat an offer that shows commitment and is accepted.

D.signal: The word 'always' turns flexible quantity into a universal failure.
D.lawyer: Requirements quantity is not always indefinite or illusory under UCC 2-306.

goldKeys.statement: A requirements term is a quantity term: it measures the buyer's quantity by actual good-faith needs, not by a fixed number.
goldKeys.unlocks: Flexible quantity treated as no quantity.

silverKeys.statement: When three choices say no contract and the stem gives a requirements phrase, cut the no-contract reasons one at a time before assuming the missing number is fatal.
silverKeys.trigger: No fixed number objection after an 'all I require' phrase.

remediation.title: Flexible quantity is not empty quantity
remediation.studentMove: Do not equate no fixed number with no quantity.
remediation.tinyRule: Requirements quantity is measured by good-faith needs.
